clue.text: Generous to burn one item of furniture

parts.note: to char something is to scorch or burn it
the Roman numeral for one
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently generous enough to set fire to a piece of their own furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generous to burn' reads as one odd phrase, but 'to' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone charitable gives freely to others, which is exactly what being generous describes; the two are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Mob with gardening tool circling road

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding
the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An angry mob armed with garden tools surrounds a road.
explanation.walkthrough: RD is the usual address abbreviation for road, and it sits inside the weeding tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large disorderly crowd of people, which is what a mob is; they are close synonyms.

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a venue is the place where something happens

explanation.surface: Someone earns money from a place that is very far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely remote' looks like 'very distant' describing the location, but it asks for the two ends of 'remote'.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in to a business or government, so it is a direct synonym of income.

clue.text: Young child to blow horn half-heartedly?

indicators.note: doing something with only half a heart means losing half of the word's middle, so one of its two central letters goes

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn

explanation.surface: A small child gives a feeble, unenthusiastic blast on a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the four-letter word is its double O; dropping half of that heart leaves one O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is an informal word for a very small child, a toddler, so it means a young child.

clue.text: Poor place for making money playing sport

parts.note: poor quality is bad
a mint is where coins are produced
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Playing sport is a poor way to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for making money' sounds like a job or business, but it is the factory that strikes coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a net, an example of a sport.

indicators.note: a piece is only part of a whole, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A finest example of Chinese writing is being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the two words: the last letter of 'Chinese' and the first four of 'literature'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the top people, so the noun stands for 'the best'.

parts.note: chaps are men
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: Men intimidate their tennis opponents with powerful serving.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'excellent service' is a tennis serve, not good customer care.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten or intimidate them with harm; the verbs are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Shrub originally planted next to metal bolt

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a rivet is a short metal pin used to fasten plates together

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a shrub beside a metal fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted' fits the shrub so naturally that it reads as part of the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is an evergreen bush widely grown for garden hedges, so it is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Competitor seen on board carrying right club?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a diver competes from a springboard or high board
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An athlete on a board carries the correct club for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship or a board game; it is the diving board. The question mark flags that 'club' is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the golf club with the largest head, used for long shots from the tee.

definitions.meaning: the arithmetic average of a set of numbers

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one description, a modestly stingy person, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for someone tight with money and the statistical term for an arithmetic average.

clue.text: Main toilet, on reflection, is ancient

parts.note: the main thing is the prime one

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that the main toilet in the house is very old.
explanation.walkthrough: Lav is the informal British word for a toilet, short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval describes the earliest ages of the world, so it means extremely old or ancient.

indicators.note: dancers move about and swap places, so the letters get moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dances to an Elvis Presley record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presley's material' sounds like his songs, but the possessive just joins the letters to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fabric used in clothing, a kind of cloth or material.

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
done skilfully is done well

explanation.surface: An author starts by neatly arranging the sources for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the English novelist and essayist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Felt bad about keeping home that's wrecked

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone feels bad about having a home that has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The regret-verb is past tense to match 'felt'; the short word for being at home slips into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruined is destroyed or badly damaged, the same state as being wrecked; the past participles are synonyms.

indicators.note: something made fresh is newly made, so the letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to try some freshly made sweet things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample' reads as a verb telling you to try the treats, but the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, which is a sample; the nouns are synonyms.

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd, unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pudding made an odd rustling noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven letters of 'rustled' make the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered pastry filled with fruit such as apple, served as a pudding or dessert.

indicators.note: confused things are jumbled and out of order, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-known scientist is muddled about something from the 1990s.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight letters of 'nineties' rearrange into the relativity scientist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein devised the theory of relativity and is the best-known scientist of modern times.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clean by rubbing hard
second meaning: low stunted bushes and vegetation

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to hose down the garden, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rubbing something hard to clean it and a noun for land covered in low bushes.

clue.text: Scheme relying upon search engine primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives up its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A plan that depends mainly on looking things up online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' looks like 'mainly' in the surface, but it picks out the first letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem meant to deceive, so it is a scheme in the sense of a crafty plot.

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the pawn is the lowliest chess piece

explanation.surface: A chess program is told to create a little pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: S for small is the label on clothing sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn something is to produce or give rise to it, as fish produce eggs, so it means to generate.

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in and keep as one's own, so one piece takes another into itself

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway faction of a larger group
RE is the British school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A hidden splinter group takes up teaching about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a subject on the British school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clandestine is kept hidden or done covertly, which is what secret means; the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: So last year hot lad worked out?

indicators.note: something worked out is put into a new form, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A handsome young man's gym routine is now out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' plays on going to the gym, which suits a hot lad, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something dated and unfashionable, which is what the slang 'so last year' means.

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back in the opposite direction
partially means only in part, so the letters are a portion of the word that follows

parts.note: three letters from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A dock worker remembers only part of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A stevedore is a docker who loads ships. 'Recalled' sounds like remembering, but it turns the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, often in praise, so it is a kind of poem.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only just within limits, on the edge

definitions.note: read cryptically as two words, a line at a frontier
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: a queue at a frontier crossing

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns the second half is a pun: split the word and a 'line' at a 'border' is a queue at customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline case is one only just on one side of a limit, so it is marginal; the adjectives are synonyms.
